_comment: Pronunciation lexicon (narration skill, PRONUNCIATION.md). Only respell and accept change narration; say/ipa/lang/sources/decoy/note/probe are the record. Looked up with lookup_pronunciation.py and probed with probe_names.py run --write on the GPU host, 2026-10-11 (voice robert, ftts 0.1.11, FrankenWhisper, 3 carriers, control + decoy). Entries whose probe found no winner carry a note with the decision and its reason. Re-probe when the voice or ftts version changes; the owner's pronunciation overrides every entry. The piece name A has no entry on purpose: narrate.py treats every word key as a name, and the article 'a' would then be checked as one. Not respelled: the script also uses 'A' as the article ('A card', 'A row'), and a respelling would apply to both. The letter was heard as 'A' (letters: ay) in 2 of 3 carriers; in 'like A in algebra' ASR wrote a lowercase 'a', which cannot tell ay from uh (the decoy 'uh' was heard as nothing). Narration triage checks every sentence where A is a piece name (ASR casing, then the vowel's length and glide).

ex-or.note: The plain spelling passed 2/3 carriers (heard 'X or', 'ex or'; once 'exorfinity' sentence-final); 'ex or' 2/3; caps EKS-or was read as letters. The script tokenizes 'ex-or' as 'ex' + 'or', and ASR writes 'X or' / 'XOR', so phrases map those back to 'ex or'. Said 29 times: every sentence is ASR-gated anyway. Decision 2026-10-11; re-probe with new respellings if QA flags it.

logarithm.note: Plain spelling PARTIAL 2/3 (once 'log aritham', mapped by phrases); Log-uh-rith-um PASS 3/3. Both are auditioned per sentence; the ASR-scored take wins.

polynomial.note: Dictionary word; the plain spelling stays first. ASR heard the plain spelling as itself in 3/3 carriers; the probe scored it UNVERIFIED only because it compares against the respelling. The respellings were heard as other words (e.g. 'Polino Miola'). Decision 2026-10-11.
